modelResponse.episodeSummary: Dorothy Chen, 79F, Atrial Fibrillation with Rapid Ventricular Response, warning, hemodynamically unstable
modelResponse.rhythm: Atrial Fibrillation with Rapid Ventricular Response (AFib RVR)
keyECGEvidence: morphology: Narrow QRS, absent P waves, fibrillatory baseline
preEventNote: Sinus tachycardia earlier in shift; converted to AFib RVR as fever spiked
modelResponse.mechanism: Systemic inflammation and catecholamine surge secondary to sepsis triggering atrial electrical instability and rapid conduction.

rejectedAlternatives.why: Troponin T is only mildly elevated (0.03 ng/mL) and ECG shows no specific ST elevation or depression beyond rate-related changes. No chest pain reported.
No specific ECG signs of PE (e.g., S1Q3T3, RBBB) are present. While tachycardia and hypoxia are present, the primary clinical picture points strongly to sepsis.
Potassium (3.6 mmol/L) and Magnesium (1.8 mg/dL) are within normal limits.

recommendedActions: Administer IV Amiodarone 150mg over 10 minutes (loading dose) for rate control, monitor for hypotension.
Administer IV Diltiazem 0.25mg/kg bolus over 2 minutes, followed by infusion 5-15mg/hr, titrate to goal HR <110 bpm, monitor BP closely.
Continue aggressive fluid resuscitation and vasopressor support (norepinephrine) to maintain MAP > 65 mmHg.
Consider echocardiogram to assess cardiac function and rule out structural causes.
Hold Amlodipine due to hypotension and bradycardia risk with rate control agents.
uncertainty: Exact source of sepsis is pending culture results.
Underlying cardiac function is unknown without prior ECG or echocardiogram.
